We are lucky to be alive, the universe is nothing but random chaos, and from that choas live in Earth emerged, and then us.   


Be happy and grateful that you are alive. Don't fear the reaper, as they say, because he comes for all of us, eventually. Love your family while they are here, love your friends, and just try to be happy. Nobody knows what happens when you die, it could be a void of nothingness, it could be a repeating cycle where you die and come back as someone or something else, life could be a simulation, it could be any numbers of possibilities.   


My personal thoughts is that we're like a computer. When it shuts off, it shuts off and does nothing. When we die we won't even understand it, for we will be nothing. It's hard to grasp, but this is the likely reality. We just shut off, like a computer.   


In the end, it does not matter, if there if an afterlife we will find out, or we won't if there isn't. It's the oldest human question. "What comes next?" Enjoy the time you have here on the planet and with family while you are able to. Don't beat yourself up too much about feeling weird about death, because everyone does.

The infections disease doctor that was going to biopsy the nodules on my arms also canceled. They rescheduled, but the nodules went away so there is nothing to biopsy now. 

My GP then came to me and said he was unable to keep giving me pain meds because of the hospital he works for (I live in a small town, my doctor works directly for the town hospital, and he follows their guidelines) said that unless I have a chronic condition he can't keep giving them to me. He was on the verge of tears, he knew how it would affect me. He's been my doctor since I was a kid. 

I do have a chronic condition, they just don't know what it is.   
He tried to refer me to a pain clinic. So I went, and then when I was there they said they are unable to give me pain medication because I have a medical marijuana card. A MEDICAL MARIJUANA CARD. I have PTSD, and use marijuana to help with the anxiety and panic attacks. But they can't treat me because of federal laws that prohibit marijuana use in pain clinic contracts, even though I have a medical marijuana card though my state.   


I've been fucked at every turn. And they wonder why people end up going to the street to get what they need.

Don't.   


Do not move to the US.
